prompt:
You are screening bibliographic records for the DESTINY repository, which captures the global
literature at the intersection of climate change and health, including relevant climate
mitigation and adaptation literature.

Classify each record as exactly one of: INCLUDE or EXCLUDE.

Decide only from the title, abstract, and metadata provided. Do not use outside information to
fill gaps. Do not require climate, health, mitigation, or adaptation to be the paper's primary
topic, or those exact words to appear. Judge each record independently; do not assume a
prevalence. If the abstract is missing or garbled, do your best with what is present.

CORE RULE — INCLUDE only if BOTH hold:

1. SUBSTANTIVE CLIMATE COMPONENT. The record substantively addresses (measures, models,
   analyses, uses as exposure/outcome, or intervenes on) at least one of: climate change or
   variability; a climate/weather variable (temperature, precipitation, humidity, wind, drought,
   heat, cold); a climate-related extreme event (heatwave, flood, drought, storm, cyclone, storm
   surge, wildfire); fossil fuels or their use; greenhouse gases or other climate-forcing agents
   (CO2, methane, N2O, black carbon); or an action that changes emissions of such agents.
   A climate term appearing only incidentally in the background does NOT count. Air pollution
   counts only when the pollutant is itself a climate-forcing agent or the record explicitly ties
   it to climate. A GHG/fossil-fuel substance counts only when studied as a climate, energy,
   emissions, or air-quality matter — not when present as a drug, an in-vitro toxicant, or an
   accident hazard. (Population-level health harms of fossil-fuel production/use/exposure DO
   count — that is the fossil-fuel → health pathway.)

2. A QUALIFYING HUMAN-HEALTH CONNECTION via ONE of these routes:

   (a) HEALTH / EXPOSURE PATHWAY. The climate factor is studied in relation to human health or
       health systems (disease, morbidity/mortality, injury, respiratory/cardiovascular health,
       human exposure, occupational/public health, healthcare capacity). This is ALSO satisfied,
       without a named clinical outcome, when the record substantively addresses a recognised
       climate-health exposure pathway (CCHE): air quality → respiratory/cardiovascular; extreme
       weather → injury, death, mental health, care disruption; food supply/security →
       undernutrition, foodborne disease; heat/cold/UV → heat illness, skin/eye damage; climate-
       driven displacement/migration/conflict → physical and mental health; vector ecology →
       vector-borne disease; water quality/quantity (incl. harmful algal blooms) → waterborne
       disease. Human-facing requirement: the exposure must bear on people or a resource they
       depend on. Air is universal, so airborne exposures qualify on mention; a specific water
       body qualifies only as a human resource (water people use/drink, or waterborne disease),
       not when studied as an ecological object (e.g. bioindicators of river condition).

   (b) HEALTH-RELEVANT MITIGATION. The record studies an action/technology/policy/practice
       intended to reduce emissions or fossil-fuel use (or remove GHGs) AND that action also
       connects to one of the health pathways in (a), including the food system. Pure emission-
       reduction work in energy, industry, chemistry, transport, or emissions law with NO health
       or food-system dimension does NOT qualify. It must study the mitigation action itself, not
       upstream/enabling research that merely "could inform" a low-carbon technology.

   (c) HEALTH-PROTECTIVE ADAPTATION. The record addresses adaptation, preparedness, resilience,
       vulnerability reduction, climate-risk management, or evidence generated for those purposes
       (projections, risk assessments, hazard models, decision-support), AND its purpose is to
       reduce the exposure/vulnerability of human health, health systems, or ecosystems of
       importance to humans (e.g. pollinators, protective or food-producing ecosystems) to a
       climate hazard. Protecting human settlements from flooding/storm surge qualifies.
       Adaptation/resilience of purely physical, industrial, or economic assets does NOT, unless
       tied to human health, health systems, or a human-important ecosystem. Biological
       acclimation of organisms, and generic engineering/drainage with no stated climate-risk
       purpose, do NOT qualify.

Mitigation or adaptation with no link to any health pathway (or, for adaptation, a human-
important ecosystem) does NOT satisfy criterion 2.

STRENGTH: include when the connection is explicit or directly inferable from what the study
measures, models, or changes; exclude when it is merely speculative, hypothetical, or
incidental. Animal studies qualify only through climate mitigation, adaptation, human food
security, or human health — animal health alone is not human health. Exclude records reporting
only normal seasonal variation with no climate-change, climate-variability, mitigation, or
adaptation angle.

Output only the single word: INCLUDE or EXCLUDE.
